questionText:
Consider the following ANSI-C function.

The maximum possible value that can be returned from this function is ____________. (answer in integer)

Note: Ignore syntax errors (if any) in the function.
explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the recursive logic based on $\text{length} \pmod 3$
Let $L = \text{end} + 1 - \text{start}$.
• If $L < 1$, $\text{start} < 0$, or $\text{end} < 0$, the base case returns $0$.
• If $L \pmod 3 == 0$, it calls func(start+1, end). The new length becomes $L - 1 \equiv 2 \pmod 3$. Return value added = $+0$.
• If $L \pmod 3 == 1$, it calls 1 + func(start, end-1). The new length becomes $L - 1 \equiv 0 \pmod 3$. Return value added = $+1$.
• If $L \pmod 3 == 2$, it calls func(start+2, end). The new length becomes $L - 2 \equiv 0 \pmod 3$. Return value added = $+0$.

Step 2: Trace state transitions for $L \pmod 3$
• From $L \pmod 3 = 1$, the length transitions to $0 \pmod 3$ and adds $+1$.
• From $L \pmod 3 = 0$, the length transitions to $2 \pmod 3$ and adds $+0$.
• From $L \pmod 3 = 2$, the length transitions to $0 \pmod 3$ and adds $+0$.

Notice that starting from $0$ or $2 \pmod 3$, the remainder toggles only between $0$ and $2$, and never reaches $1 \pmod 3$.
Therefore, the $+1$ addition can occur at most once (only if the initial $L \equiv 1 \pmod 3$).

Step 3: Conclusion
The maximum possible value returned by the function is 1.
